label: prf:wigner-coefficient-derivation
title: Proof of wigner coefficient derivation
html:
The isospin Casimir T^2 commutes with all \sigma_i (it lies in the center of H_n). By Schur's lemma, T^2 acts as a scalar c_\lambda on each irreducible representation \lambda.

The Markov trace of the Casimir over the complete H_5(R, q):

  \mathrm{tr}_M(T^2) = \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot c_\lambda

By Frobenius reciprocity, the isospin Casimir at H_5 induced from H_3 has eigenvalue T(T+1) in each component, weighted by \dim_q(\lambda)^2.

The step from this trace to the coefficient is not derived here: the proof asserts that the coefficient is the Hecke-level scale at k = 5,

  [5]_q! = [1]_q [2]_q [3]_q [4]_q [5]_q ,

the q-factorial at level 5 (Markov-trace normalization). The identification of the Bethe--Weizsäcker Wigner term with this coefficient is the content of the conjecture the proposition is conditional on, and the choice k = 5 is an input, not an output of the argument. Only the algebraic product expansion of [5]_q! \cdot m_e is unconditional.

At level k, the coefficient is [k]_q! \cdot m_e.

The numerical comparison with the fitted liquid-drop Wigner coefficient is a comparison against a fitted value and is not part of this proof.
